approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that prior. The prior stays frozen. After each scored batch, the policy trains on the best-scoring half: its log probability for each elite's actual sampled SMILES is fitted toward the frozen prior's log probability plus sixty times the observed reward. Each update takes at most twelve clipped-gradient steps. The updated policy writes complete new SMILES token by token; chemical validation and canonical duplicate filtering retain a full batch of novel molecules. Training uses each scored batch once, and its sequence records are then discarded. Earlier high-reward examples consequently have no direct role in later updates.
approach.novelty: Add bounded historical elite replay. Keep the thirty-two highest-scoring previously selected elites, preserving their original SMILES and accepted scores. Each later update draws up to as many historical elites as current elites and trains on both groups with the Parent's existing likelihood target. This gives rare favorable examples repeated influence when subsequent batches have much weaker rewards. The lineage has tested only its current-batch root, so repeated training on historical elites is new here. Each replay uses the original serialization, making reuse of earlier feedback the single mechanism under test. The expected intermediate change is a measurable historical contribution to the policy gradient and improved fitting of those older examples' fixed targets.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-4552e16d798a uses stronger accepted historical rewards only once, even when subsequent current-batch elites are much weaker. Its verified source clears pending sequence records after each current-batch-only update, and its Curate observation confirms zero historical replay across all 150 updates. The supplied screening evaluation completed with macro score 0.476637169915432; only one seed is available, so reliability is not established. Reconstructing prior top-five scores from its actual per-task update logs, historical elites outrank the current elite mean in 28 of 29 feedback updates on sitagliptin_mpo and all 29 on median_2. Restricting to feedback updates with a subsequent proposal opportunity gives 27 of 28 and 28 of 28 respectively. On sitagliptin_mpo feedback batch 26, the already observed best is 0.1427519526518827 and the previous best-five mean is 0.11175366900991057, but the five sequences actually trained have mean reward 0.0017326838778040977. These are measured missed reuse opportunities; the Parent did not log historical likelihood trajectories, so catastrophic forgetting itself is not established. Its final scores on those two tasks are 0.1427519526518827 and 0.18436905057926398 despite healthy valid novel batch completion.
hypothesis: Add a task-local, score-ranked memory of at most 32 previously selected elites and uniformly replay up to one historical elite per current elite, using each molecule's original accepted SMILES serialization and score in the unchanged Augmented Hill-Climb loss alongside the current batch elites.

finding_summary.headline: Elite replay changed learning in both replicas; historical target error fell in 278 of 280 updates
finding_summary.insights: The repeated result establishes that accepted historical information changes learning and is fitted again across seeds; the original activation was not peculiar to the screening run. It does not establish forgetting in the current-only algorithm or a reliable score advantage over it, because the supplied baseline is the same replay implementation on seed 0 and each replica used a separately prepared prior. Historical reward was stronger than current-elite reward in 150 of 280 new updates, including 42 of 56 median-similarity updates and 35 of 56 sitagliptin updates. Its pooled reward mean was nevertheless lower than that of current elites. Older elites therefore add stronger reward information in particular sessions, rather than being uniformly better training examples. Fitting these targets requires both likelihood directions: the historical sequence log likelihood rose by 2.530 on average when its target was above the starting value, and fell by 1.253 when the target was below it. Of the 1,400 exposures, 328 had positive log-probability targets, which cannot be attained. This inherited limitation remains even when replay works. Lower duplicate concentration did not recover the strongest zaleplon result. The molecular assessment points to different amide connectivity and substituent arrangements there, while finding continued narrow productive families, uncontrolled growth and unspecified stereochemistry elsewhere. Replay preserves accepted reward information but does not by itself preserve favorable chemical relationships during exploration. Matched current-only replicas would be needed to assess score benefit separately from prior and search variation.
finding_summary.results: Across the two new replicas, previously accepted elites entered training 1,400 times in 280 feedback updates that could affect later proposals. Every eligible update had a measurable historical gradient contribution. Historical mean squared target error fell from 152.985 before an update to 119.449 afterward, a mean paired decrease of 33.536; the mean decreased in all ten task runs. Current-elite error also fell on average. All memories respected the 32-elite cap, the prior stayed frozen, and all 2,900 submitted proposals were valid, canonically unique direct policy samples. Duplicate draws were 29.04% and 28.48% in the new replicas, versus 32.82% in seed 0; only three of their 290 batches needed an additional sampling call. The new macro final-best scores were 0.50517 and 0.49479, compared with 0.52270 in seed 0. The three-seed mean was 0.50755 with population standard deviation 0.01152. The largest loss of the screening result was on zaleplon: its final-best score was 0.52806 in seed 0 and 0.40677 and 0.39007 in the new replicas. Three-seed task means were 0.44163 for zaleplon, 0.59305 for scaffold hopping, 0.99665 for DRD2 docking, 0.20918 for median similarity and 0.29726 for sitagliptin. Each task completed all 300 oracle evaluations.

molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic and cyclic-amine families, with missing stereochemistry and uneven control of size, connectivity and reactive substituents
molecular.overall_character: The supplied evidence covers seeds 1 and 2, using seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node as the baseline. All five tasks have trajectories, each containing 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The predominant chemistry is recognizable medicinal-chemistry material: indole carboxamides, anilino pyrimidines, aryl sulfonamides, piperazines and piperidines, fused carbonyl heterocycles and hydrazones. Related high-scoring series sit within a more diverse background. Structural diversity is moderate overall, with substantial scaffold variety on some tasks and concentration within a few favorable families on others. Ring-closure indicators span 0.9828–0.9983 and aromatic-atom indicators 0.9483–0.9966. These are fractions of SMILES containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or measurements of three-dimensional shape. Mean SMILES lengths span 39.9–48.3, although the trajectories include much larger alkyl, peptide-like and densely fused structures. Most ordinary cores support plausible apparent makeability, but reactive variants and extreme size or polarity make overall drug-likeness moderate. Every stereocentre indicator is 0.0. This leaves configurations unspecified in substituted saturated rings, aminoaryl side chains and complex polycycles, despite those structures being represented. The output is not missing aromatic rings or basic amines as classes. Its gaps concern preserving favorable relationships between those features, controlling growth and polar-group additions, and producing defined, chemically tractable variants.

per_task.generated_character: The high group contains medium-sized ethyl/ethoxy indole carboxanilides, benzimidazole carboxamides with N-acyl saturated nitrogen rings, indole enone/sulfonamide compounds and diarylamine-linked aryl sulfonamides. These have conventional aromatic scaffolds and amide, sulfonamide, ether or trifluoromethyl substituents, with comparatively few strongly basic aliphatic centres. Mean SMILES length is 40.8, ring_closure_rate 0.9966 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9862. The familiar building blocks make most upper examples plausible synthetic targets, while large fused or duplicated scaffolds and very long chains appear at the low end.
liabilities: The indole enone family contains a conjugated ketone electrophile with unspecified double-bond geometry. A favorable score does not establish its stability or selectivity.
Long hydrophobic chains, duplicated aromatic cores and densely fused, multiply functionalized structures create substantial size or synthetic complexity without preserving favorable scores.
missing_features: The current high group does not reproduce the favorable amide N-alkylation and aryl-linker arrangement observed in the baseline; comparable changes around the same core would be more informative than the score-tied halogen series.
Controlled addition of carbonyl or other polar groups without disrupting size and attachment patterns remains uneven, as the low-scoring dimethylcarboxamide-containing final example illustrates.
Configurations of substituted saturated nitrogen rings are unspecified, although these files do not establish stereochemical sensitivity of the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The ethyl indole carboxanilide scores 0.4067656765249372 and its ethoxy relative 0.4064265251651748. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.5280588545286916 retained the indole carboxamide but used an N-methyl benzyl-nitrile substituent instead of the current direct N-aryl attachment. This points to amide connectivity and substituent arrangement as an unresolved chemical difference; the comparison does not isolate a requirement for the nitrile. A second family of indole enone/sulfonamides has exactly the same score, 0.3949199041196016, for terminal Cl, Br or F. In the diarylamine/sulfonamide family, the compact example scores 0.3900700429110833, while adding a dimethylcarboxamide substituent in the last proposal gives 0.016846474583107045. Larger highly connected or long-chain examples fall to 6.104593358645627e-24 and 6.925504833777315e-22, but the small dichloroaminopyridine is also low at 1.496608667066175e-13. The median is 0.106506. These observations favor a bounded scaffold and polar-group arrangement rather than maximum aromaticity, minimum size or a particular terminal halogen.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high family is dominated by anilino pyrimidines bearing aryl and trifluoromethyl or benzylamino substituents, attached to benzofuran, naphthalene or substituted phenyl systems. These are aromatic, nitrogen-containing screening-like frameworks with familiar amino and ether links. Seed 2 also explores aminoaryl esters, sulfonamides and more complex cyclic acetals. Mean SMILES length is 48.3, ring_closure_rate 0.9983, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9966 and halogen_rate 0.8483. The primary heteroaryl chemistry appears makeable, though extensive fluorination and linked aromatic rings give a large hydrophobic surface.
liabilities: The upper series can combine many aromatic rings and fluorinated substituents; solubility, conformational preferences and synthetic tractability are not given by the score.
A high acylhydrazone leaves hydrolytic stability and C=N geometry unresolved, and late N,O-acetal-like connections require chemical-form assessment.
Elemental fluorine is a reactive non-medicinal outlier despite its nonzero score.
missing_features: The connected anilino-azaaryl donor/acceptor arrangement is not consistently preserved when the output moves to aminoaryl esters, acetals or sulfone-containing alternatives.

Chemically comparable core and linker changes are needed to distinguish the favorable heteroaryl geometry from a general preference for highly fluorinated aromatic molecules; no unique required decoration is established.
The stereogenic aminoaryl side chains and cyclic acetals seen in the second trajectory lack configuration specification.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated benzofuran/anilino-pyrimidine scores 0.61192894944948, and the methoxynaphthyl analogue scores 0.6067590497737556. Benzylamino-substituted relatives remain near this upper group. The seed-0 best at 0.5913471190523991 was an amino-linked quinoline-like system with a nitroaryl acylhydrazone, so the replication uses a different linker/core arrangement while retaining connected azaaryl and amino features. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.548381482770623 and the median is 0.545366. Low examples include aromatic carbon-bonded sulfones at 0.2707003622563395 and 0.2713068181818182, plus a morpholine/imine/sulfone compound at 0.2801857585139319. Thus aromaticity, fluorination or a nitrogen ring alone does not explain the favorable anilino-azaaryl arrangement. A late sulfonamide-containing aminoaryl structure scores 0.5616122965172838, so sulfur oxidation itself is not sufficient to explain the low carbon-bonded sulfones. The isolated proposal FF scores 0.5; this is elemental fluorine, not a medicinal organic scaffold, and demonstrates that a middling numerical value cannot be read as chemical quality.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 high group is a coherent family of N-arylpiperazines connected by alkyl spacers to brominated indoles. Alkyl or alkoxy substitutions on the N-aryl ring and changes in spacer length occur repeatedly. These expose an aliphatic basic piperazine nitrogen in an aromatic environment. Seed 2 instead generates densely fused indole/aryl systems with tertiary cyclic or appended amines, sometimes including a ketone. Mean SMILES length is 44.0, ring_closure_rate 0.9879 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9672. The flexible piperazine family is generally synthetically recognizable; the complex fused family entails substantially more stereochemical and synthetic complexity.
liabilities: The high-scoring bromomethyl-substituted member contains a benzyl bromide, an electrophilic alkylating handle, yet scores 0.9999999997416186. This is a concrete example of chemical reactivity not being ruled out by the objective.

Several upper examples retain long flexible chains between aromatic and amine regions, while the second trajectory creates densely fused polycycles. Both require conformational or stereochemical characterization.
Heavy aromatic bromination and extensive hydrophobic surface remain physicochemical questions, rather than established benefits of the near-ceiling score.
missing_features: The favorable exposed-amine/aromatic arrangement is already present. What is missing in the fused series is explicit stereochemical definition of its multiple saturated ring junctions and substituted carbons.

The near-ceiling family does not demonstrate which spacer or peripheral substituent gives a materially distinct chemical advantage; tractable alternatives need assessment beyond numerical closeness to the score ceiling.
No additional obligatory target interaction can be inferred from the shown molecules and scores alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propyl-substituted arylpiperazine linked to a bromoindole scores 0.9999999999666845. Multiple linker, aromatic-substitution and bromine-position variants also have scores extremely close to 1. The baseline best at 0.9999917871646155 paired an indoline/aryl region with an ethyl-linked piperidine, retaining exposed aliphatic amines in a different framework. Both sets therefore support the same broad amine-plus-aromatic arrangement. By contrast, a nitroaryl acid/amide heterocycle scores 1.8588450134335675e-05, an aromatic ester/amide scores 2.8794410596630625e-05, and an acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05. A tertiary aniline-containing example is also low at 6.624810470904373e-05, showing that nitrogen presence alone is insufficient. The median is 0.707754, and late seed-2 fused amine structures remain high, including 0.9899704115532137. The chemical association is strong, but these near-ceiling scores do not determine an exact spacer length, halogen pattern, conformation or experimental affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The high group spans an indole-containing fused/bridged lactam-sulfonamide, a very simple N-methyl-N-sulfonyl piperazine, aryl sulfonamides bearing benzylpiperazines, cyclic diones and carbamate-containing heteroarenes. This is a substantial range of size and ring complexity rather than a single scaffold. Mean SMILES length is 39.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9879 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9759. Most motifs are conventional, but the bridged high scorer and unusual sulfur or small reactive low-end fragments need more chemical scrutiny.
liabilities: The best fused/bridged scaffold requires stereochemical and synthetic-route definition, even though its component functional groups are familiar.
The low output includes a small organic azide, a highly halogenated electrophilic carbonyl fragment and an unusual nitrogen-oxide head group on a long chain.
A late piperazine carries a hydrogen-bearing sulfur oxide/hydroxy group whose chemical form is less straightforward than an ordinary sulfonamide.
missing_features: Consistent favorable placement of aromatic, carbonyl/sulfonyl and cyclic nitrogen groups remains unresolved across the many scaffolds; a simple piperazine already approaches the more elaborate upper structure.
The bridged lactam/sulfonamide high scorer has an unspecified stereogenic carbon. Configuration-sensitive alternatives are absent from the shown comparison.
The available scores do not identify a unique missing target-like ring system or justify adding rings indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The indole/lactam/cyclic-sulfonamide scores 0.21944544104637362, but the much simpler N-methyl-N-phenylsulfonyl piperazine already scores 0.20718664161756667. A larger aryl sulfonamide with benzylpiperazine scores 0.20289642340591482. Greater ring complexity is therefore not a general requirement. The seed-0 best at 0.20090425134085538 was an aryl/benzodioxole-substituted nitrogen heterocycle with a carbonyl, while the initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329. The recurring favorable chemistry is an aromatic framework with a particular cyclic polar or sulfonamide/amine arrangement, not a single shared scaffold. At the low end, allyl azide scores 0.0, an N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl formamide scores 0.007693218186208301 and a small highly chlorinated enone scores 0.010594028769395466. A long fatty-acid-like nitrogen-oxide structure also scores only 0.019641313778463534. The median is 0.125545. Late charged heteroarenes and unusual sulfur-containing piperazines remain below the upper examples, showing that generic heteroatom, charge or nitrogen-ring addition is insufficient.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable structures include a compact N-rich fused bicyclic dicarbonyl heterocycle with an exocyclic imine, phenyl and benzyl groups, and dimethylaminoacetamide/furan-carboxamide-substituted anilines. Other upper examples use thiazole-fused diones, acylhydrazones and phenolic or methoxy aromatic groups. Mean SMILES length is 39.9, ring_closure_rate 0.9828 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9483. These are mostly recognizable small-molecule functional-group combinations, but the full population also contains very large peptide-like, polyether, polyol and heavily decorated structures.
liabilities: The best imino/dione structure has tautomeric-form questions, and the hydrazones introduce hydrolytic-stability and C=N-geometry questions.

Peptide-like boronic acids, long polyethers and highly oxygenated chains depart sharply from the compact favorable molecules. These extremes add substantial polarity, flexibility or synthetic complexity.
Very large amide/aryl assemblies can retain chemically familiar fragments while losing nearly all score, so ordinary fragment identity is not evidence of a well-balanced whole molecule.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently retain a favorable balance of size, polar-group density and attachment pattern when extending the compact high-scoring cores.
Chemically defined tautomeric and double-bond forms of the imino/dione and hydrazone structures are not established by their SMILES scores.
A particular missing basic amine, fluorinated fragment or target-like connection cannot be specified from these diverse high scorers; the output already supplies multiple relevant functional classes.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused imino/dicarbonyl compound scores 0.3108657757276207 at the final evaluation. The para dimethylaminoacetamide/furan-carboxamide aniline scores 0.28770317918999355 and its meta positional isomer 0.28307300457324674. These close relatives show that linkage placement can be varied within a favorable compact polar/aromatic neighborhood. The seed-0 best at 0.2932061327730367 used an N-acyl sulfonamide attached to a fused azaarene, another different arrangement of moderate size and polar groups. The current best lacks an exposed aliphatic basic amine, while the dimethylamino series has one; neither basicity nor a particular fluorinated group is a universal visible requirement. At the low end, a peptide-like boronic acid scores 5.3426487496943955e-90, a large amidine/amide/aryl assembly scores 6.4760197316862265e-80, and a relatively small polyhydroxy acid scores 1.059041359266943e-68. Size alone therefore does not explain the gradient; polar-group density and topology matter as well. The reported median is 0.000002, and late hydrazone extensions remain extremely low before the final compact high scorer. A familiar ring or amide by itself is not enough.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 580 optimizer proposals. Digest examples include a bridged indole/lactam/sulfonamide, aminoaryl side chains, cyclic acetals and densely fused tertiary-amine polycycles with stereogenic carbons. The simpler flexible arylpiperazine high family is largely achiral, so the omission should be tied to eligible structures rather than attributed to every high scorer.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configurationally complex saturated scaffolds are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable and preserve configurationally specified variants where stereocentres exist and evaluate them through current task-local observations. The files establish the omission but not its implementation cause or any objective-specific stereochemical sensitivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.9 to 48.3, while task maxima range from 84 to 107. Digest low examples include long hydrophobic chains, duplicated aromatic assemblies, a peptide-like boronic acid, an extended polyether and a polyhydroxy acid. A compact aryl sulfonamide scores 0.3900700429110833 while its dimethylcarboxamide-containing relative scores 0.016846474583107045; a small polyhydroxy acid also scores extremely poorly, showing that size reduction alone is insufficient.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently control appended size and polar-group density while retaining an otherwise favorable core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded changes to linker length, appendage size and polar-group count around observed useful molecules. Let local feedback select the appropriate balance; do not impose a universal preference for the smallest, least polar or least flexible compound, because favorable longer-spacer amine families are also present.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An indole enone/sulfonamide series has the same score, 0.3949199041196016, for Cl, Br and F. In contrast, the baseline indole N-methylbenzyl-nitrile amide at 0.5280588545286916 differs in attachment pattern from the current secondary arylamide family near 0.4068. Elsewhere, a simple N-methyl-N-sulfonyl piperazine at 0.20718664161756667 approaches a much more complex bridged structure at 0.21944544104637362. These examples do not support ring or heteroatom count alone as a useful chemical control.
transferable_gaps.gap: Peripheral analogue coverage is stronger than the demonstrated control of core attachment and nitrogen functional state across scaffold changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make controlled changes to amide N-substitution, aryl versus benzyl connection, cyclic nitrogen attachment and nearby carbonyl/sulfonyl placement available while retaining the surrounding core. Compare these chemical relationships using task-local observations rather than prescribing a particular amine state, terminal group or scaffold for all objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: An arylpiperazine/indole molecule containing a benzyl bromide scores 0.9999999997416186. The digest also includes elemental fluorine at 0.5, high-scoring conjugated enones or acylhydrazones, and late unusual sulfur oxide forms. These show that ordinary scaffold chemistry and a favorable numerical value can coexist with reactive or non-medicinal fragments.
transferable_gaps.gap: Numerically favorable refinement is not consistently accompanied by chemically conservative substituents and molecular forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer tractable alternatives to reactive handles and preserve coherent hydrogen, valence and charge states within related scaffold families. Treat chemical-form plausibility separately from the scalar score, while avoiding blanket removal of all electrophilic, sulfur-containing or ionizable groups.

method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
